verdict: UnitedHealth Group's profit rebounded sharply — earnings from operations up 52% to $6.6B — even though revenue slipped 0.4%, because it spent less on medical care and ran the business more cheaply while serving fewer members.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: $112.7B in revenue, vs $113.2B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $2.59 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $4.69

kpis.label: Medical care ratio
kpis.note: Share of premiums paid out as medical care — down from 89.9% a year ago

kpis.label: Earnings from operations
kpis.note: Up 52% vs $4.3B a year ago — Optum $3.7B, UnitedHealthcare $2.8B

segments.name: Premiums
segments.note: Health-insurance premiums from members, employers and government programs — the money people pay for coverage. It fell as membership shrank to 48.3M people.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Prescription drugs and other products sold, mainly through Optum Rx pharmacies — the fastest-growing revenue line this quarter.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Fees for delivering care and for health technology and data services, mainly from Optum Health clinics and Optum Insight.

segments.name: Investment and other income
segments.note: Income from the company's investment portfolio and other small sources.

opex.name: Operating costs
opex.note: The day-to-day cost of running the company — people, technology and offices. At 12.8% of revenue, it improved from 13.5% a year ago.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: A non-cash charge spreading the cost of buildings, equipment, software and acquired businesses over their useful lives.

takeaways.title: Profit rebounded while sales stood still
takeaways.text: Earnings from operations jumped 52% to $6.6B and earnings per share rose to $4.56 from $2.59, even as revenue dipped 0.4% to $112.7B. The recovery came from spending less — on medical care and on running the company — not from growth. The company also raised its full-year 2026 outlook to at least $19.50 per share, or $20.50 on an adjusted basis.

takeaways.title: Medical costs finally came down
takeaways.text: The medical care ratio — the share of premiums paid out as medical care — improved to 88.4% from 89.9% a year ago, and medical costs fell about $3.0B to $77.0B. Pricing and benefit changes helped, as did $610M of favorable reserve development: care in 2026 cost less than the money set aside for it.

takeaways.title: Fewer members — and Optum out-earned the insurer
takeaways.text: UnitedHealthcare served 48.3M people, down from 50.1M a year ago: Medicare Advantage membership is down 935,000 since year-end and Medicaid rolls keep shrinking as eligibility is rechecked. Optum contributed $3.7B of the $6.6B operating profit vs UnitedHealthcare's $2.8B, helped by Optum Health swinging from $41M to $735M.

oneTimers: Below operating earnings, UnitedHealth booked a $76M loss on subsidiaries held for sale, tied to the remaining South American businesses it is exiting; the nine-month total on that line is $209M.

Operating profit includes gains the company strips out of its 'adjusted' figures: $224M at the operating level from portfolio sales and South American items (gains on businesses sold, partly offset by losses on the remaining South American operations) and $74M of restructuring and other items, including a $95M reduction in loss-contract reserves.
otherDetail: Other expense of $1,039M is $963M of interest expense plus a $76M loss on subsidiaries held for sale (mainly the remaining South American businesses). Investment income is not in this line — it is already counted in revenue.
footerNote: Net earnings of $4,300M include $190M belonging to noncontrolling interests; $4,110M is attributable to common shareholders.
